verifications.claim: President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi in April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Pam Bondi’s swift dismissal on Thursday" (R1, dated Apr 02, 2026); "fired her Thursday" (R2); "announced Thursday that he was ousting Pam Bondi" (R4, Apr 02); "fired Attorney General Pam Bondi on Thursday" (R5); "fired her via social media post" (R6); "Trump has fired Pam Bondi" (R7, Apr 02)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the firing by Trump in April 2026, with specific dates aligning.

verifications.claim: Attorney General Pam Bondi's tenure was 14 months.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "ending a tumultuous 14-month tenure" (R4); "ends a turbulent 14-month term" (R5); "14-month tenure as attorney general" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements in R4 and R5 specify exactly 14 months.

verifications.claim: Pam Bondi was replaced on an acting basis by Todd Blanche.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "replaced by Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, serving as the acting attorney general" (R2); "named Todd Blanche... to take over as acting attorney general" (R4); "replacing Ms. Bondi with Todd Blanche, her deputy, on an interim basis" (R5); "replaced for now by Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, who will serve as acting attorney general" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state Blanche as acting replacement.

verifications.claim: President Trump was frustrated over Pam Bondi's failure to aggressively prosecute his political enemies.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "unable to make progress on prosecuting his enemies" (R1); "hadn’t been aggressive enough at delivering wins in investigations against Trump’s political foes" (R2); "frustrated him with her struggles to prosecute his enemies" (R4); "failed efforts to prosecute his political enemies" (R5); "not investigated or prosecuted enough of his political opponents" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly link Trump's frustration to insufficient prosecution of enemies, matching 'failure to aggressively prosecute'.

verifications.claim: President Trump was frustrated over Pam Bondi's "limited success" in acting on his grievances.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "frustrated him with her struggles to prosecute his enemies and her handling... her pace — and limited success — in overseeing efforts to target his rivals" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: R4 uses the exact phrase 'limited success' in context of acting on grievances/prosecuting rivals.

verifications.claim: President Trump was dissatisfied with Pam Bondi's performance.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "grown dissatisfied with Attorney General Pam Bondi" (R2); "not satisfied with her job performance" (R4); "continuing dissatisfaction with her performance" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements of dissatisfaction with her performance across sources.

verifications.claim: President Trump was dissatisfied with the pace of investigations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "No one is more anxious than Trump to get everything done immediately" (R2); "frustration with Bondi’s pace — and limited success" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention frustration with pace/speed of investigations and actions.

verifications.claim: President Trump was dissatisfied with Pam Bondi's handling of Epstein-related files.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "over the way she handled the Epstein files" (R1); "struggled... with the Epstein files saga" (R2); "her handling of the Epstein files" (R3); "handling of files related to... Jeffrey Epstein" (R4); "handling of the Epstein files" (R5); "handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Consistent direct references to dissatisfaction with Epstein files handling.

verifications.claim: President Trump was annoyed by Pam Bondi's inability to secure indictments against perceived enemies, including cases involving former FBI Director James Comey and NY Attorney General Letitia James.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "cases against Comey and James... dismissed"; "failure to move past those safeguards" (R1); "Failing to secure indictments"; cases against "James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James" dismissed (R2); "failed efforts to prosecute... Comey and... Letitia James"; "cases... thrown out" (R4); "inability to secure indictments of people he referred to as 'scum'" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify frustration over failed indictments/ prosecutions of Comey and James specifically.

verifications.claim: President Trump felt Pam Bondi failed to fully "execute on his vision".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "he doesn’t think she 'executed on his vision' way that he wanted" (R2)

verifications.claim: President Trump felt Pam Bondi failed to manage the Justice Department as a tool for retribution.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "could not fully deliver on the president’s mercurial wishes" (R1); "transformed the Justice Department into a tool for avenging the president’s grievances but frustrated him" (R4); "satisfying Mr. Trump’s appetite for retribution"; "tried desperately... to pursue politically motivated investigations" but "came up short" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe DOJ as tool for retribution/revenge, Trump's frustration with her insufficient delivery, but not exact phrasing of 'manage as a tool'.

verifications.claim: President Trump wanted a more aggressive approach.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "she didn’t go far enough" (R1); "hadn’t been aggressive enough at delivering wins" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Direct implications of wanting greater aggression in prosecutions/investigations.

verifications.claim: President Trump considered replacing Pam Bondi with more combative, trusted allies.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Considering "Lee Zeldin"; other names like "Jeanine Pirro" (combative figures, trusted allies) (R2, R4, R7); "floated the idea of replacing Ms. Bondi with Lee Zeldin" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm considering replacements like Zeldin and combative allies (Pirro, etc.), implying desire for more effective/trusted, but not explicitly 'more combative'.
